original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected reproduction command and choose a single replay stage for profiling.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Speed up the T16 invoice boundary audit by reusing parsed JSON for byte-identical input files while returning fresh mutable values; retain the full 54-case receipt.
scope_change_reason: Takes the remaining repeated-JSON-parsing lead of Kumagi PR3009 after checking that the compression optimization is already on main.
bottleneck_link: Faster complete boundary replays improve review throughput without dropping source binding or any admission predicate.
stop_rule: Stop after same-fixture timing and complete receipt comparison, with changed-input and mutable-return controls; abandon acceleration if it is not beneficial.
evidence: RESULT.json: four fresh Python 3.12.15 processes in baseline/cached/cached/baseline order; all complete 54-case receipts byte-identical to the original. Mean wall time 188.516 -> 174.954 seconds (7.19% lower locally), mean peak RSS 939848 -> 970356 KiB. Cached runs reuse 488 of 628 reads; ten invalidation/value-isolation controls pass. Shared-host timing ranges overlap; no portable speedup claim. Registered package replay also passed on Python 3.12.15.
author: thakrarsagar with OpenAI Codex
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in implementation, profiling, tests, source inspection and writing; parallel read-only source review and separate regression-test implementation. No independent human review claimed.

open_questions.question: Does this reader reuse improve replay on another supported Python 3.12 host?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The observed speedup depends on interpreter, CPU and competing load; mathematical coverage does not.
open_questions.first_step: Run the baseline and cached commands in alternating order, compare full receipts and report elapsed time and peak memory.
open_questions.blocked_by: No correctness blocker; independent host measurements are not included here.

submission_refresh.finding: No competing T16 reader-cache PR or claim found; predecessor compression optimization already incorporated. No matches is not a novelty certificate.
